classification.difficultyReason: Read integer coordinates, including points on axes, and count points using coordinate signs.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Give the coordinates of each of the points $A$ to $G$ below.

spec.description: Square-unit Cartesian grid spanning x=-6 to 8 and y=-5 to 7, with positive-direction axis arrows, no axis titles, numbered ticks and seven labelled points. Source red markers and grey grid become ordinary black marks under house style. Width increased for tick and point-label readability.
spec.mathematics: A=(1,1), B=(2,-3), C=(0,6), D=(-4,0), E=(-4,-2), F=(-4,5), G=(4,-4). Horizontal labels -5 through 7, including 0; vertical labels -4 through -1 and 1 through 6.
spec.answerVisibility: All plotted points and their letter labels are permanent givens. Coordinate-pair answers are hidden in the question edition.

answer.worked:
Read the horizontal coordinate first and the vertical coordinate second. Points on the vertical axis have horizontal coordinate $0$; points on the horizontal axis have vertical coordinate $0$.

$$\begin{aligned}A&=(1,1)\\B&=(2,-3)\\C&=(0,6)\\D&=(-4,0)\\E&=(-4,-2)\\F&=(-4,5)\\G&=(4,-4)\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many of these coordinates have

answer.worked: $A$, $B$ and $G$ lie to the right of the vertical axis, so their $x$-coordinates are positive. There are $3$ such points.
$B$, $E$ and $G$ lie below the horizontal axis, so their $y$-coordinates are negative. There are $3$ such points.
